items.title: Repo merge-method contradiction: main ruleset allows only squash, repo flags allow only merge — API merges 405 both ways
items.body:
## Repo merge-method contradiction: `main` ruleset allows only squash, repo flags allow only merge — API merges 405 both ways

Discovered merging PR #9267 (approved, CI green, CLEAN): the merge policy's two authoritative sources contradict each other, deadlocking every non-bypass API merge.

**Evidence (2026-09-28):**

- Ruleset `main` (active, `updated_at` 2026-09-26T17:33Z): `required_linear_history` + `pull_request.allowed_merge_methods: ["squash"]`.
- Repo settings: `allow_merge_commit: true`, `allow_squash_merge: false`, `allow_rebase_merge: false` (the #9105 merge-commit default; appears flipped ~2026-09-27T23:00Z, i.e. *after* the ruleset's last update — PR #9246, merged 2026-09-27T23:10Z as the only post-flip merge commit, looks like a bypass-actor merge).
- `merge-pr.sh --auto` (resolves method `merge`) → `HTTP 405: Merge commits are not allowed on this repository`.
- `merge-pr.sh --merge-method squash` → `loom-daemon forge merge-method` (validated against the repo-flags triad, `loom-daemon/src/forge_merge_method.rs`) refuses: `allowed method(s): merge`.

**Impact:** every `merge-pr.sh`/Champion API merge on this repo fails until reconciled. PR #9267 is parked approved-but-unmergeable (handoff comment posted there).

**Remedy (operator, one of):**

1. Update the `main` ruleset's `pull_request.allowed_merge_methods` to `["merge"]` to match the #9105 flag intent, **or**
2. Re-enable `allow_squash_merge` in repo settings to match the ruleset.

Follow-up worth considering (separately): `loom-daemon forge merge-method` validates against the repo-flags triad only and ignores ruleset `allowed_merge_methods` — worth teaching it the ruleset source so the validator and the endpoint can't disagree like this.

**Approved.** Reviewed in a checkout of the `feature/issue-8191` worktree (`.loom/worktrees/issue-8191`).

**Scope check** — the diff collapses the three near-identical `#4186/#6694/#6264` remove-vs-preserve blocks in `merge-pr.sh`'s post-merge worktree cleanup into `_worktree_cleanup_decide <kind> <path>`, backed by the new pure `loom_daemon::merge_pr::worktree_preserve::decide`/`render` reached via `loom-daemon merge-pr worktree-preserve`. Confirmed both forge/git reads (`_issue_is_closed_for_cleanup`, `branch_has_landed`) stay in the shell, and the Rust side takes no stdin/network/git — it's a pure function of its `Context` args.

**Fail-direction verified directly in code**: `_worktree_cleanup_decide`'s guard —
```bash
if [[ $rc -ne 0 || ( "$action" != "REMOVE" && "$action" != "PRESERVE" ) ]]; then
  warning "... Preserving rather than guessing REMOVE ..."
  return 0
fi
```
— correctly defaults to PRESERVE on any daemon fault (missing binary, older daemon, off-protocol output). Exercised locally by Test 7's case T5 in `test-merge-pr-worktree-path.sh` ("a daemon predating the verb preserves rather than guessing cleanup"), which passed.

**Retired assertions**: 5 `assert_grep`s (not the 2 I was initially told to expect — the PR body itself correctly says "Five") were retired via the established `retired()` convention (printed, counted, never silently deleted), each naming the property, why it's structural (the message text is now a Rust format literal, nothing shell-shaped to grep), and a real, specific successor (the differential test's per-kind cases plus named unit tests in `worktree_preserve::tests`). This matches the convention used elsewhere in this test family (`test-merge-pr-primary-worktree-guard.sh`, `test-merge-pr-partial-increment.sh`, etc.).

**"Part of #8191" convention**: correct — this is a partial-increment slice in the ongoing `merge-pr.sh` port, consistent with the ~20 prior slices' pattern (verified against `defaults/roles/builder-pr.md`'s `Closes` vs `Part of` guidance).

**Coherence of inherited work**: the PR is a single clean commit (`32b1ecf2c`) with no evidence of a half-integrated leftover from the interrupted prior session — history and diff are coherent.

**Verified locally** (real `target/release/loom-daemon` built from this branch):
- `defaults/scripts/tests/test-merge-pr-worktree-path.sh`: 57/57 passed.
- `cargo test -p loom-daemon --release --lib merge_pr::worktree_preserve`: 9/9 passed.
- `scripts/check-file-size-budget.sh --list`: `1035 defaults/scripts/merge-pr.sh` (claimed 1035, ceiling 1071) — confirmed exactly.
- `scripts/check-shell-allowlist.sh`: OK (fixture declared, `test` category).
- `scripts/check-daemon-subcommand-versions.sh`: OK.

**CI**: all required checks (`Structural Checks`, `Shell Syntax (macos-latest)`, `Daemon Checks`) pass, and `Rust Linting & Build Check` (which runs `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `cargo clippy -D warnings`) passed, confirming those claims. `Rust Unit Tests (1/3..3/3)` and `Native Port Suites` all green. The one red check, `Rust OTLP Feature Tests (1/3)`, is `isRequired: false` (confirmed via the GraphQL `isRequired` field — `mergeStateStatus` is `UNSTABLE`, not `BLOCKED`) and fails in `merge_pr_partial_reset_differential.rs`, a file/module this PR does not touch at all; the same commit's non-OTLP `Rust Unit Tests` partitions all pass, and the last 5 `main` CI runs were green, matching the OTLP-job-only flake pattern already tracked in (closed) #8683. Filed a follow-up for it: #9278 — not blocking this PR.

Formal-review reconciliation (`check-review-feedback.sh`) reports `CLEAR` at this head SHA.

Nice work — this is a clean, well-tested slice with the fail-safe direction properly preserved on a data-loss-adjacent code path.

9276.author: loom-fleet-dispatch-1[bot]
9276.body:
**Merge blocked — repo-wide merge-method config drift, not a PR content issue.**

`./.loom/scripts/merge-pr.sh 9276 --auto` failed:
```
Error: Failed to merge PR #9276: {"message":"Merge commits are not allowed on this repository.","documentation_url":"...","status":"405"}
```

Root cause: this repo's branch ruleset for `main` requires `required_linear_history` + `allowed_merge_methods: ["squash"]` (set by `scripts/install/setup-branch-protection.sh`, unchanged), but the repo-level merge-strategy toggle now says `allow_merge_commit: true, allow_squash_merge: false, allow_rebase_merge: false` (flipped by #9115's `setup-repository-settings.sh` default change to prefer merge commits). The two are mutually incompatible: `forge_detect_merge_method`/`loom-daemon forge merge-method` read the repo-level toggle and resolve to `merge`, but GitHub rejects `merge` because of the ruleset's `required_linear_history` — and an explicit `--merge-method squash` retry is refused by `loom-daemon forge merge-method` itself ("allowed method(s): merge"), because it also only reads the repo-level toggle. **Every merge in this repo is currently blocked**, not just this PR.

This is out of scope for this sweep to fix (it's a live repository-settings change on the org's main repo). Filed as a follow-up for operator attention: see the linked issue. This PR's `judge-done` sweep checkpoint is left intact so the next sweep pass retries the merge automatically once the config is reconciled.

The #8248 required-check-freshness guard blocked the merge of PR #9276: a required check's green result predates the current base-branch tip, and this repo's merge token has no `actions:write` to re-run that check directly. This moves the head SHA, which invalidates the standing Judge approval (#5686). Expect this PR to cycle back through `loom:review-requested` once CI on `00e681e` completes, then merge normally once re-approved.

The #8248 guard itself is unchanged and still applies to the next merge attempt.
